experiences.company: FURG - Federal University of Rio Grande
experiences.role: Full Stack Developer & Research Fellow (CNPq Scholarship)
experiences.description: As a CNPq research fellow, I did something unusual: I built production web applications while researching network security. Most developers focus on one or the other. I did both, and that combination changed how I think about building software. I developed the e-COO platform with React and Next.js while investigating how internet routing protocols can be exploited. This work resulted in published research and taught me that understanding infrastructure makes you a better application developer.
achievements: Built full-stack production applications with React, Next.js, TypeScript, Express.js, and Tailwind CSS
Published two peer-reviewed papers on BGP routing security and prefix hijacking vulnerabilities
Presented research at ERRC 2023 (Regional School of Computer Networks) at UFRGS
Received 'Destaque' (Distinguished Work) award for outstanding undergraduate research
Presented findings at FURG's 32nd Scientific Initiation Congress and 22nd MPU
Researched how attackers exploit BGP routing to redirect internet traffic—knowledge that shapes how I think about system security
Learned that most developers build apps assuming the network is safe. My research taught me it's not.

experiences.description: I investigated how the internet's fundamental routing protocol—BGP—can be weaponized. Prefix hijacking sounds abstract until you realize it's how attackers can redirect entire networks' traffic. I analyzed these vulnerabilities, documented attack patterns, and published my findings in peer-reviewed conferences. This research earned a Distinguished Work award, but more importantly, it taught me to think about security from the infrastructure up, not just the application layer down.
achievements: Researched BGP routing vulnerabilities and prefix hijacking—how attackers exploit the protocol that holds the internet together
Analyzed Autonomous System behaviors and documented network security implications
Published research in SBC (Brazilian Computer Society) proceedings—peer-reviewed, not blog posts
Presented findings at ERRC 2023, a regional computer networks conference at UFRGS
Received 'Destaque' award recognizing outstanding undergraduate research
Developed network infrastructure expertise that most web developers never touch—and it shapes every architectural decision I make
